subject: Privileged support access — post-discovery recap & evidence ask
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@skyhawk.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Privileged support access — post-discovery recap & evidence ask

Jordan / Becca — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap of what we covered on the call and the concrete items we need to validate to move forward with a Dedicated/Private plan (knowing this will be tied to your contract and SOC2/procurement timeline):

1) Scope & residency
- You confirmed that EU customer workloads must remain in eu-west-1 and PII for EU customers cannot be replicated outside that region.
- Action: please confirm the list of customer clusters that will need EU residency (company IDs or account names).

2) PII handling & retention
- Skyhawk requires redaction on ingest for names/emails and a 30-day raw retention window for troubleshooting (then redacted/aggregated logs kept for 13 months).
- Action: please send your PII classification table (column mapping) or sample dataset schema so we can propose a retention + redaction flow.

3) Support access, RBAC & break-glass
- We walked through Redwood support roles: Support Viewer, Support Operator, Support Escalation. You asked for a JIT break-glass procedure with audit trail and time-limited elevation.
- Action: please provide the list of Skyhawk IAM groups/roles and the names of two pilot support users for an initial simulation.

4) Audit logs & evidence
- You asked for sample audit events (session start/stop, role elevation, command list) and retention guarantees.
- Action: we'll share a small audit sample extract from a sanitized test tenant; please confirm accepted fields.

5) Procurement & timelines
- Procurement (procurement@skyhawk.ai) is targeting contract execution by 2026-12-15. We should complete the technical validation and a break-glass tabletop by 2026-12-07 to stay on that path.

Attachments: support-runbook-template.pdf (high-level runbook we referenced) — I attached a stub.

Next steps (proposed):
- Jordan/Becca: send PII mapping + pilot support users by EOD Tuesday (2026-11-24).
- We (Redwood): provide RBAC mapping template and sanitized audit sample by 2026-11-25.
- Schedule a 60-min tabletop with your security ops and our ops on 2026-12-02 or 12-07.

If any of the asks above are off, call it out — otherwise I’ll treat this as the checklist for the technical validation.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

---

(On the call)
Becca: "break-glass needs to create a non-repudiable audit trail; we can't accept undocumented access."
Jordan: "we need to make sure support sessions are auditable across both hosted and dedicated modes."

From: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@skyhawk.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Becca Lim <becca.lim@skyhawk.ai>, procurement@skyhawk.ai
Date: 2026-11-23T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Privileged support access — post-discovery recap & evidence ask

Thanks Mina — good recap. Confirming a few things from our side: 

- Residency: yes, EU customers must be pinned to eu-west-1 and no raw copies outside that region. For the first cut, attach list: "Skyhawk-Prod-EE-1" and "Skyhawk-EE-Analytics" (we'll provide full list tomorrow).
- PII: we prefer redaction-on-ingest for email addresses and SSN-like fields. For troubleshooting we can agree to a 30-day window for reversible data and then irreversible redaction.
- Support access: we want RBAC mapping that aligns with our internal groups (sky-support-read, sky-support-ops, sky-priv-esc). We can provide the pilot user accounts: jcole and blim.
- Audit: a sample of event fields is OK; procurement will need confirmation on retention SLAs.

Procurement note: procurement@skyhawk.ai — can we get the SOC2 Type II and encryption-at-rest evidence sent into the DocuSign/attachments area? We want the security packet by 2026-11-27.

Happy to lock in the tabletop on 2026-12-07 at 10:00 PT if that works for your ops team.

—Jordan
Jordan Cole
Head of Security Operations, Skyhawk AI
jordan.cole@skyhawk.ai | +1 (650) 555-0133

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T11:07:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Privileged support access — notes + evidence checklist (internal)

Looping in Sean for ops validation. Internal checklist / asks for the Skyhawk packet (we'll send to Jordan/procurement):

- RBAC mapping deliverable: use redwood-rbac-mapping.xlsx (attached) — fields: RedwoodRole, SkyhawkGroup, DefaultTTL, ApprovedEscalators (list of internal users).
- Break-glass runbook: must include (a) approval path, (b) one-click JIT elevation TTL default 15 minutes, (c) automatic session recording + immutable audit export. Draft runbook and attach to the Drive link.
- Audit sample: provide a sanitized JSONL export with these event types: session_start, session_end, role_elevate, role_revoke, api_call (with redaction markers).
- Data residency proof: short design note describing our per-tenant region pinning and confirmation that no async backups replicate outside the region for pinned tenants.

Operational questions for Sean:
- Can we commit to a sanitized audit sample by 2026-11-25?
- Can we run an internal break-glass simulation against a demo tenant and capture the audit artifacts by 2026-12-03?

Attachments: redwood-rbac-mapping.xlsx (template)

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Jordan / Becca / Procurement — thanks for the confirmations. Quick status and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Deliverables shipping tomorrow (2026-11-26):
- Redacted audit sample JSONL (sanitized) — will include session_start/session_end/role_elevate events with redaction flags.
- RBAC mapping template (completed) — redwood-rbac-mapping.xlsx attached.

2) Tabletop date: we booked the break-glass tabletop for 2026-12-07 10:00 PT (invite will come from calendar). Please confirm that jcole and blim will attend and that procurement can be on the invite for any contract clarifications.

3) On residency: we'll write a short design note confirming per-tenant region pinning and backup behavior; expect that in the same packet.

4) Evidence: we will include a pointer to SOC2 Type II (redacted dates) and the KMS/HSM encryption summary in the security packet. Procurement — if you prefer DocuSign/secure upload, let me know and we’ll route there.

5) Break-glass simulation: we propose a staged sim on 2026-12-03 (internal) and the customer-facing tabletop on 2026-12-07. Goal: capture audit artifacts and demonstrate TTL revocation.

If that timeline works, we’ll produce the packet tomorrow and loop in Solutions Eng for the tabletop prep.

Thanks — Mina
